wording: Tax year: the calendar year 2026 (Veranlagungszeitraum 2026). A company with a financial year that does not match the calendar year is taxed on the profit of the financial year that ends in 2026 ([§ 7(4) KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__7.html)). A German company pays three taxes on its profit: corporate income tax, the solidarity surcharge on that tax, and municipal trade tax. This skill covers the first two in full and summarises the third. For the trade tax method, use `de-trade-tax`.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF20, German corporate income tax (Körperschaftsteuer): 2026

wording: - **Resident companies (unlimited tax liability).** A company is taxed in Germany on its worldwide income if its place of management (Geschäftsleitung) or its registered seat (Sitz) is in Germany ([§ 1(1) and (2) KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__1.html)). This includes the GmbH (and its UG variant), the AG, the SE, the KGaA, cooperatives, other private-law legal persons, and commercial businesses of public bodies. "Place of management" means the centre of top-level management ([§ 10 AO](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__10.html)); the seat is the place named in the articles ([§ 11 AO](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__11.html)). A foreign-registered company run from Germany is therefore fully taxable here.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF24, Who this applies to

wording: - **Non-resident companies (limited tax liability).** A company with neither its management nor its seat in Germany is taxed only on German-source income ([§ 2 no. 1 KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__2.html)). The main case is a German permanent establishment (Betriebsstätte): any fixed place of business, such as a branch, office, workshop, warehouse, or a building site lasting more than six months ([§ 12 AO](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__12.html)). A treaty may narrow this.

wording: **Trade tax in one paragraph.** Every GmbH or AG is a trade business in full ([§ 2(2) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__2.html)). Trade income starts from the corporate tax profit, then adds back part of financing costs (interest, rent, leases, royalties above a EUR 200,000 allowance) and makes reductions (for example dividends from holdings of at least 15%). It is rounded down to full EUR 100, multiplied by 3.5%, then by the multiplier of each municipality where the company has an establishment. At a 400% multiplier the trade tax is 14% of trade income, which with 15.825% gives 29.825% in total. Multipliers differ widely by town: always read the client's own notice. A company gets no credit for trade tax against corporate tax (the § 35 EStG credit is for individuals only). Method, add-backs and reductions: see `de-trade-tax`.

wording: - **Interest.** Withholding under § 43 EStG covers specific types, for example convertible bonds, profit-participating bonds and profit participation rights ([§ 43(1) no. 2 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__43.html)), at 25%. Ordinary loan interest paid to a foreign lender is not in that list, but check the lender's limited tax liability under § 49 EStG before paying gross. Interest between associated EU companies can be relieved under [§ 50g EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__50g.html) (Interest and Royalties Directive).
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF114, Cross-border points

wording: - **Royalties.** Payments to a non-resident for the use of rights or know-how bear 15% withholding ([§ 50a(1) no. 3, (2) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__50a.html)) plus 5.5% surcharge ([§ 3(1) no. 6 SolzG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/solzg_1995/__3.html)). Relief through § 50g EStG, a treaty, or a BZSt exemption certificate. Where a treaty applies and the payments to that recipient in the calendar year are not more than EUR 10,000, the payer need not withhold but must still file the withholding return (§ 50c(2) no. 2 EStG).
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF115, Cross-border points

wording: - **For the non-resident recipient,** corporate tax on income subject to withholding is generally settled by the withholding, unless the income belongs to a German business ([§ 32(1) KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__32.html)).
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF116, Cross-border points

wording: - **CFC rules (Hinzurechnungsbesteuerung).** If German taxpayers control a foreign company, its passive income is added to their German income where it bears tax of less than 15% ([§ 7 AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__7.html), [§ 8(5) AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__8.html)). The test compares the foreign tax with 15%, not with the German rate, so the 2028 to 2032 rate cuts do not change it. Refer any CFC case.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF117, Cross-border points

wording: - **Exit tax for companies.** If Germany loses or restricts its right to tax the gain on an asset (for example the asset moves to a foreign PE), the company is treated as selling it at fair market value ([§ 12(1) KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__12.html)). For a move to an EU or EEA state the company can apply for a compensating item released over five years ([§ 4g EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__4g.html)). Shareholders who leave Germany: see `leaving-germany-exit-tax`.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF118, Cross-border points

wording: A holding and trading GmbH has, for 2026, profit before tax of EUR 3,000,000. This includes a EUR 200,000 dividend from a German GmbH in which it has held 20% since 2020. It has unused losses carried forward of EUR 4,000,000 for corporate tax and, by assumption, also EUR 4,000,000 for trade tax. No change of shareholders in the last five years, so § 8c does not bite. Assumed multiplier 400%. No other add-backs or reductions.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF166, Example 2: losses brought forward plus a dividend from a subsidiary

wording: 1. **Participation exemption.** The holding was at least 10% at the start of 2026, so the dividend is exempt: deduct EUR 200,000, add back 5% = EUR 10,000. Income before losses: EUR 2,810,000.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF168, Example 2: losses brought forward plus a dividend from a subsidiary

wording: 2. **Corporate tax loss offset.** First EUR 1,000,000 in full. Then 70% of the EUR 1,810,000 above it = EUR 1,267,000. Total offset EUR 2,267,000. Taxable income EUR 543,000. Losses left: EUR 1,733,000.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF169, Example 2: losses brought forward plus a dividend from a subsidiary

wording: 3. **Corporate tax and surcharge.** 15% of EUR 543,000 = EUR 81,450. Surcharge 5.5% = EUR 4,479.75.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF170, Example 2: losses brought forward plus a dividend from a subsidiary

wording: 4. **Trade tax.** Trade income starts from the same EUR 2,810,000. The dividend is already out through § 8b, and the 5% add-back stays in trade income ([§ 9 no. 2a sentence 4 GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__9.html)). Loss offset: EUR 1,000,000 plus **60%** of EUR 1,810,000 = EUR 2,086,000. Trade income EUR 724,000; base amount at 3.5% = EUR 25,340; trade tax at 400% = EUR 101,360. Trade tax losses left: EUR 1,914,000.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF171, Example 2: losses brought forward plus a dividend from a subsidiary

wording: 5. **Total** for 2026: EUR 187,289.75, even though the company still has losses on both accounts. This is the minimum taxation effect.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF172, Example 2: losses brought forward plus a dividend from a subsidiary

wording: 1. **Where is the company managed, and where are its establishments?** This decides German residence, and the trade tax multiplier of each municipality (with its year). Several towns means the base amount is split.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF211, Ask the client first

wording: 2. **What is the financial year?** A non-calendar year changes which profit falls into 2026 and when prepayments are due.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF212, Ask the client first

wording: 3. **Is a Steuerberater filing the return?** It moves the deadline from 2 August 2027 to 29 February 2028, unless the tax office orders earlier filing.
destination: Exact wording retained; current LF213, Ask the client first

wording: 4. **What shareholdings does the company hold, how large, and since when?** At least 10% at 1 January for the corporate tax dividend exemption; at least 15% at the start of the period for the trade tax reduction; 12 months for § 43b relief on dividends it pays out.

wording: 5. **Have more than 50% of its own shares changed hands in the last five years, or is that planned?** Losses may be forfeited under § 8c KStG.

wording: 6. **What is the net interest expense, and is the company part of a group or tax group?** At EUR 3m or more the interest barrier applies; an Organschaft changes who is taxed.
